title: Working at Google – what employees say (Session 5)
text: Google is famous for a very selective hiring process, freedom to work on personal projects, luxurious offices with free food and services, and the feeling of belonging to an elite.

In a 2015 discussion thread on Quora, about forty current and former employees described the downside. Managers were often promoted for technical brilliance rather than leadership skills and were seen as distant. Workloads were heavy; e-mails arrived at midnight and few people really switched off at weekends or on holiday – stress, burn-out and broken relationships were mentioned.

With more than 50,000 employees, Google felt bureaucratic to some (weekly goal reviews, validation processes); many said that unless you are a star engineer you are just one cog in a huge machine. Because everyone is “great” and many are overqualified, it is hard to stand out, be challenged or get promoted quickly. Others criticised conformism: the same profile from the same universities, an echo chamber where challenging the official line is not welcome.
